focus: Which of the twelve serial deep-loop files actually need serial execution
noveltyJustification: 5 of 7 findings are new facts about the serial set's composition and its timing bounds; the 157 s figure is reused from the packet and the saving is a derived estimate.
keyQuestions: Which of the 12 serial deep-loop files actually need serial execution, and what would shrink that group?
What sets the time of the cli lane's tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts, and can it be cut without dropping assertions?
Where do the roughly 300 s of import time in the spec-kit core lane come from, and which parts can be cut?
Do the ledger read-caching ideas (singleWriterReadCache, gateway rescans) buy measurable time, and what runtime risk do they carry?
Which remaining cuts still pay off on a smaller CI runner, and how should each be measured before it is claimed as a win?
answeredQuestions: Which of the 12 serial deep-loop files actually need serial execution, and what would shrink that group?
ruledOut: Removing db-open-close from the serial set: its purpose is a lock race
Removing lineage-timestamp-window from the serial set: 60 s child bound is a real timing dependency
Merging the seven 7-line stress wrappers: no measurable saving
Treating child spawning as a reason to stay serial: only upper-bound assertions are load-sensitive
